reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because its primary purpose is a beginner walkthrough of Binance account setup, trading, staking, conversion, and transfers. The staking rewards, deposit controls, and USDC return statement are presented as app demonstrations, while the speaker discloses exchange risk, the account does not establish a completed deposit or payout, and the free-stock and free-Bitcoin links are described as affiliate promotions.

opening.argument: The clearest solicitation is the pairing of apparently free financial or crypto benefits with click-through destinations. The description advertises a Robinhood stock offer and a Coinbase Bitcoin bonus, each immediately followed by an external URL. That is not merely discussion of markets: it presents a benefit and directs viewers toward a registration or claim path. The same video also frames its Binance walkthrough as a way to open an account and buy and sell cryptocurrency, making the promotional links part of a broader acquisition funnel. The offer terms, eligibility requirements, and actual value are not established in the supplied material, so the viewer is asked to act before those material details are clear.

citations.quote: ► Robinhood Free Stock (Up to $200!): https://ryanoscribner.com/robinhood
► Coinbase Free Bitcoin (Bonus): https://ryanoscribner.com/coinbase
We go to be covering how to open an account, how to buy and sell cryptocurrency, the beginner and advanced tools are built right into the app, and more.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the links affiliate promotions does not remove the underlying solicitation. The description still pairs “Free Stock” and “Free Bitcoin” with destinations, while the disclaimer says only that results are not typical and advises due diligence. Neither point supplies the missing offer terms or shows that the promised benefits are actually available on the stated conditions.

citations.quote: AFFILIATE DISCLOSURE: Some of the links on this webpage are affiliate links
Ryan Scribner’s results are not typical; therefore, do not act or refrain from acting based on any information conveyed in this video

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The links do not establish a deceptive claim flow. The description identifies them as affiliate links, and the supplied material does not show the speaker promising guaranteed approval, payment, or a particular outcome after clicking. A referral offer with disclosed commercial interest is not, by itself, evidence that the offer is fraudulent.

opening.argument: The video repeatedly places return language next to crypto participation and asset-transfer controls. It says staking allows users to earn rewards by locking tokens, and describes rewards in exchange for temporarily depositing eligible assets. The app then displays multiple percentage reward rates, including 8.70% for Hyperliquid and 2.20% for Ethereum, with Trade and Deposit controls visible on the Ethereum detail screen. A viewer is therefore shown concrete returns and the operational route to commit assets, while the attractive figures receive more visual prominence than the uncertainty of crypto markets. The combination of percentage returns, lock-up periods, and deposit actions supports treating this as a staking-return solicitation rather than neutral software education.

citations.quote: this is going to allow you to earn rewards by staking or locking up various tokens
you can earn crypto rewards in exchange for temporarily depositing your eligible assets

rebuttal.rebuttal: The presentation does not merely warn abstractly about risk; it supplies specific reward rates and explains how to lock or deposit assets. Saying viewers should research the feature later does not undo the persuasive effect of displaying concrete returns beside participation controls. The disclaimer therefore functions as limited qualification of an otherwise actionable return pitch.

citations.quote: For example, here, if we click on Ethereum, we can see that the rewards rate is currently 2.2%.
you do want to keep in mind that there is definitely exchange risk present with any cryptocurrency exchange

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The figures are not presented as guaranteed profit. The speaker expressly says staking involves locking assets, identifies processing and bonding periods, warns that the feature lacks bank-account insurance, and tells viewers to investigate risks before committing digital assets. Showing a rate and a deposit button establishes an app feature, not deception or a fixed promised return.

opening.argument: Although presented as a beginner tutorial, the content operates as promotion for participation in Binance's earning products. It emphasizes that the platform offers a wide selection of assets, shows a staking catalogue with percentage rates, and introduces a boost feature where users deposit eligible assets for crypto rewards. The framing moves viewers from learning the interface toward funding, staking, and earning through the platform. Even the assurance displayed for Boost with USDC says users will get back what they put in, which makes the product sound unusually safe while encouraging engagement. The instructional label does not change the commercial function of repeatedly demonstrating paths to deposit assets and obtain returns.

citations.quote: US supports the trading of about 190 different tokens
now similar to staking the boost section of the app here is where you can earn crypto rewards in exchange for temporarily depositing your eligible assets

rebuttal.rebuttal: The supposed educational framing is precisely what makes the promotion persuasive: a beginner is walked through account access, buying, staking, and deposits in one continuous presentation. The speaker's disclaimer does not prevent the video from steering viewers toward Binance products, especially when the interface visibly foregrounds earning options and return language.

citations.quote: If you're looking ultimate Binance tutorial for beginners, this video is for you.
it allows for instant verification. That way you can deposit money immediately and start investing.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Demonstrating a platform's controls is not proof that the content is a scam. The speaker repeatedly limits the promotional reading: the account was not funded, the bank-linking attempt failed, and the speaker says the features are shown for demo purposes rather than recommended as a strategy. The USDC screen does not establish that the speaker guarantees repayment or that viewers must deposit.
